sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A bulbous perennial reaching about 50 cm. Its broad basal leaves appear before a flowering stem topped by an umbel of white flowers. It grows mainly in cool, shady woodland; its native range extends from western and central Europe to the Caucasus.

sections.title: Food and lookalikes
sections.text: Wild garlic is eaten, particularly for its leaves. These can be confused with lily-of-the-valley (Convallaria majalis), autumn crocus (Colchicum autumnale) and arum (Arum maculatum), which are toxic. These plants are identification lookalikes, not edible substitutes.
